obligation: Holding company (business associate) notice to Health Care Services
trigger: The holding company discovers a breach of unsecured PHI it handles for Health Care Services (EHR access through SYS-G1)
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery; the BAA requires 10 days
notify: Health Care Services HIPAA Privacy Officer
clock_starts: Discovery by any holding company employee or agent (164.410(a)(2)); Day 0

obligation: Plan sponsor report to the group health plan
citation: 45 CFR 164.314(b)(2)(iv) (plan document term, to be adopted under POAM-022); 164.504(f)(2)(ii)(D); POL-03 4.4
trigger: Security incident or improper disclosure involving plan PHI held by the sponsor
deadline: Same day (group policy); the plan's own breach clock runs from the sponsor's knowledge

obligation: Third-Party Service Provider notice to the insurers
citation: Model #668 sec. 6D; 2017 intercompany agreement (security schedule pending, POAM-016)
trigger: Cybersecurity event in the holding company's systems involving the insurers' nonpublic information
deadline: Immediately on the bridge (no contract term yet); the insurers' own 72-hour clock starts the day after actual knowledge

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice (worked example)
trigger: Holding company maintains personal information on behalf of another group entity (employer subsidiaries, insurers, Health Care Services)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, but no later than 10 days following the determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred; must give the entity all information it needs for its notices
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred

obligation: Health Care Services breach notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI after the four-factor assessment
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery

obligation: Health Care Services notice to HHS (500 or more)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals
deadline: Contemporaneously with individual notice (within 60 days of discovery)
notify: HHS Office for Civil Rights (breach portal)

obligation: Health Care Services media notice
trigger: More than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Prominent media outlets in Florida (about 1,200 patients)

obligation: Group health plan breach notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of unsecured plan PHI (appeal files) after the plan's own four-factor assessment
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery

obligation: Group health plan notice to HHS (500 or more)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals
deadline: Contemporaneously with individual notice

obligation: Group health plan media notice
trigger: More than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Prominent media outlets in Florida (about 1,400 members)

obligation: People who are both plan members and clinic patients
trigger: An individual's PHI was involved in both breaches
deadline: Each covered entity's own clock
notify: Affected individuals (one coordinated letter may name both entities)
notifying_entity: Health Care Services and the group health plan

obligation: HIPAA breach log to HHS (fewer than 500)
trigger: Breach affecting fewer than 500 individuals
deadline: Within 60 days after the end of the calendar year

obligation: Law enforcement delay
trigger: Law enforcement states notice would impede an investigation
deadline: Delay for the period stated in writing; up to 30 days if oral and documented

obligation: Insurance commissioner notice: Alabama
citation: Model #668 sec. 6A as enacted (Ala. Code 27-62-1 to 27-62-12, per the NAIC state page); text varies, counsel confirms
trigger: 250 or more Alabama consumers and the event must be reported to another government body or is reasonably likely to cause material harm
deadline: As promptly as possible and no later than 72 hours after determination
notify: Alabama Commissioner of Insurance (electronic form as directed)
clock_starts: Determination; for events at a Third-Party Service Provider, the day after notice or actual knowledge (sec. 6D(2))

obligation: Insurance commissioner notice: South Carolina
citation: Model #668 sec. 6A as enacted (S.C. Code 38-99-10 to 38-99-100, per the NAIC state page); text varies, counsel confirms
trigger: 250 or more South Carolina consumers and the reporting criteria are met
deadline: As promptly as possible and no later than 72 hours after determination

obligation: Insurance commissioner notice: Tennessee (unverified: state text not reviewed)
citation: Tenn. Code 56-2-1001 to 56-2-1011 (portions of Model #668, per the NAIC state page)
trigger: As enacted in Tennessee; counsel confirms which notice provisions were adopted
deadline: As enacted; plan to the model's 72-hour clock until counsel confirms
notify: Tennessee Commissioner of Commerce and Insurance

obligation: Commissioner notice content and updates
trigger: Commissioner notice is required
deadline: With the initial notice, then updated as information becomes available

obligation: Copy of consumer notice to the commissioner
trigger: Commissioner notice was required and consumers are notified under the state breach law
deadline: When consumers are notified

obligation: Notice to producers of record
trigger: Affected consumers bought through independent producers
deadline: As soon as practicable as directed by the commissioner
notify: Producers of record (about 2,400 agencies; affected subset)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - many affected policies sold through agencies

obligation: Insurers in states without the model (Florida, Georgia, North Carolina)
citation: State breach notification laws (Florida worked example: Fla. Stat. 501.171)
trigger: Breach of personal information of state residents
deadline: See state rows below
notify: Affected residents; state regulators where the state law requires

obligation: State breach notification laws (all entities)
citation: Laws of each state where affected individuals reside
trigger: Breach of personal information as each state defines it
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where required; consumer reporting agencies above state thresholds
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - employees in 31 states; claimants in 6 states
notifying_entity: Each employing entity, each insurer, Health Care Services, the plan

obligation: Florida notice to individuals (worked example)
trigger: Breach of security involving Florida residents' personal information
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach (up to 15 more days with good cause given in writing to the Department within 30 days); a HIPAA-compliant notice is deemed compliant if a copy is timely provided to the Department
notify: About 61,000 employees, 238,000 claimants, 1,200 patients, 1,400 plan members in Florida

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: 500 or more Florida individuals
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach (the 15-day extension does not apply to this notice)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: More than 1,000 Florida individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incident)
trigger: The disclosure committee determines the incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination (delay only on a U.S. Attorney General determination)

obligation: SEC Reg S-K Item 106 annual disclosure
trigger: Annual report
deadline: Next Form 10-K

obligation: Bank recall and fraud reporting
trigger: Fraudulent payments released
deadline: Immediately on discovery
notify: Paying banks' fraud desks; FBI IC3

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement and CISA
citation: FBI field office or IC3; CISA
trigger: Criminal intrusion
deadline: As soon as practicable (Day 0-2 target)

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any extortion payment
trigger: Any payment demand is considered
deadline: Before any payment
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party); law enforcement

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Any Severity 1 incident
deadline: Per policy; call the carrier hotline before engaging vendors

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - NOT YET IN EFFECT (final rule not published as of 2026-09-25)

obligation: Federal Reserve notification incident
trigger: Notification incident at a bank holding company
deadline: No later than 36 hours after determination
applies_at_this_tier: No - not a bank holding company (12 CFR 225.2(c)(1))
